definitions.explanation: Doing something while showing resistance or lack of enthusiasm. Implies going along with something despite not wanting to.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はしぶしぶ{承諾|しょうだく}した。
しぶしぶながら{手伝|てつだ}ってくれた。
{子|こ}どもはしぶしぶ{宿題|しゅくだい}を{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The child reluctantly started their homework.

notes:
MIMETIC ORIGIN:
Reduplicated form related to {渋|しぶ}い (astringent, reluctant). The repetition emphasizes the reluctance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- しぶしぶ{承諾|しょうだく}する - to agree reluctantly
- しぶしぶ{従|したが}う - to comply unwillingly
- しぶしぶ{受|う}け{入|い}れる - to accept grudgingly
- しぶしぶながら - albeit reluctantly

POSITION IN SENTENCE:
Appears before the verb, modifying the manner of action.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {嫌々|いやいや} - unwillingly (stronger negative feeling)
- {仕方|しかた}なく - having no choice
- {渋々|しぶしぶ} - alternative kanji spelling
